lecture_context.lecture_title: Lecture 3: Full Cycle of a Deep Learning Project

unit.name: AI project lifecycle is driven by code plus uncertain data
unit.description: Frames the lecture as a practical walk-through of a full deep-learning project, emphasizing why data makes AI development more empirical than traditional software.
unit.summary: AI projects differ from traditional software because engineers control the code but do not fully know what is in past or future data [ts=78s]. The face-recognition example makes the uncertainty concrete: lighting, hair, glasses, expressions, scarves, and future real-world inputs can all affect behavior [ts=103s]. The lecture expands the project cycle beyond model training to problem specification, data collection, model design, training, deployment, monitoring, and maintenance [ts=347s]. Because surprising data properties appear only after trying a system, ML development is an empirical loop of design, train, analyze, and update [ts=539s].

key_points.text: AI projects combine code with data, and the data is hard to predict or control.
Unknown data properties such as lighting, glasses, hair, facial expression, or winter scarves can determine system behavior.
A full ML system includes specifying the problem, getting data, designing and training a model, deploying, monitoring, and maintaining it.
The core development loop is design the model, train it, analyze results, then update the model or data.

kp_catalog.name: AI projects as empirical systems
kp_catalog.description: AI systems are developed empirically because performance depends on code plus data whose contents and future distribution are not fully known.
kp_catalog.importance_rationale: This idea frames the whole lecture: unlike ordinary software, ML projects require build-test-analyze loops because data creates unpredictable behavior [ts=78s] [ts=146s].

kp_catalog.name: Full machine-learning project lifecycle
kp_catalog.description: A practical ML system requires problem specification, data, model design, training, deployment, monitoring, and maintenance, not only model training.
kp_catalog.importance_rationale: The lifecycle list is the lecture's organizing scaffold and is revisited through data collection, deployment, monitoring, and maintenance [ts=347s].
